**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 21 of the MSA already delivers our preferred LOL-CAP position, and in one respect exceeds it:

| Playbook requirement | Document | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Mutual cap | § 21.1 "each Party's total aggregate liability"; "The cap is mutual" | ✅ |
| Greater of 12 months' fees / USD 1M | § 21.1 verbatim, using **"paid or payable"** (not just "paid") | ✅ |
| Mutual exclusion of indirect damages | § 21.2 "neither Party is liable for indirect… consequential" | ✅ |
| Uncapped carve-outs | § 21.3 "Excluded Claims" — confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other party's IP | ✅ |
| Customer payments not "damages" | § 21.3 final sentence | ✅ |

Two points worth noting for the deal file:

- **The cap base is real, not illusory.** "Fees" (§ 1.5) captures recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the 12-month multiplier has genuine substance. The exclusion of a one-time implementation charge is mitigated by the USD 1,000,000 floor, which protects us in a low-spend first year.
- **§ 21.2 is better than our model language.** It deems restoration of Customer Data, replacement services, breach notifications and incident response to be *direct* damages. That closes the usual gap where a vendor concedes an uncapped data-breach carve-out but then argues the actual response costs are excluded consequential damages. We should resist any vendor attempt to trade this sentence away in later rounds.

I also confirmed no competing cap is buried elsewhere: searches for "liability" and "exceed" surfaced only the § 18 insurance limits and § 22 audit-cost provision, and §§ 19–20 contain no aggregate-liability or sole-remedy cap — § 20.5's refund remedy is expressly "in addition to" Vendor's defence obligations, so the IP indemnity remains uncapped via § 21.3.
